title: Discrete Diffusion Models via Evolving Variational Autoregressive Networks
abstract: Conventional score-based diffusion models learn scores without representing normalized densities, whereas tractable normalized models support both sampling and direct likelihood evaluation. A recent tensor-network approach provides such a representation but is largely restricted to low-dimensional lattices. Here we introduce a discrete diffusion model that parameterizes normalized probability distributions using variational autoregressive networks. Explicit Markov jump operators govern the forward noising and reverse denoising dynamics, extending discrete diffusion models with normalized distributions to spin systems on higher-dimensional lattices. We apply this framework to the two- and three-dimensional Ising models across ordered, critical, and disordered regimes, accurately computing thermodynamic quantities including free energy, energy, and magnetization. We further integrate the framework with Monte Carlo sampling, using adaptive diffusion steps to maintain high acceptance rates even at low temperatures while enhancing sample diversity. These results establish a neural-network framework for the discrete diffusion model with normalized probability distributions.
summary: This paper presents a novel discrete diffusion model utilizing Variational Autoregressive Networks (VAN) to accurately parameterize normalized probability distributions for spin systems. By applying this framework to the 2D and 3D Ising models, the authors successfully compute key thermodynamic quantities across different phases. This establishes a powerful, scalable neural-network approach for statistical mechanics simulations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a discrete diffusion model capable of parameterizing normalized probability distributions, overcoming limitations in both conventional score-based models and low-dimensional tensor-network approaches.
main_result: They introduce a framework using Variational Autoregressive Networks (VAN) that successfully models normalized distributions for spin systems on higher-dimensional lattices, allowing for accurate computation of thermodynamic quantities.
method: The core method involves training a VAN to approximate the target Boltzmann distribution, governing the forward noising and reverse denoising dynamics via explicit Markov jump operators.
model_or_system: The model is applied to spin systems, specifically the two- and three-dimensional Ising model, whose target distribution follows the Boltzmann distribution $P(\sigma) \propto e^{- eta E(\sigma)}$.
key_observables: Free energy, energy, and magnetization per site.
important_parameters: Inverse temperature $ eta$ (spanning ordered, critical, and disordered regimes); lattice dimensions (2D and 3D).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the use of the variational autoregressive factorization $P_	heta(\sigma) = \prod_{i=1}^D P_	heta(\sigma_i | \sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_{i-1})$ to decompose the joint probability.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by defining the VAN-based discrete diffusion model, details the dynamics using Markov jump operators, applies it to the Ising model across various regimes, and integrates the method with MCMC sampling techniques.
why_interesting: The integration of advanced deep learning (autoregressive networks) with established statistical physics tools (Ising models, MCMC) provides a powerful, generalizable computational framework for analyzing complex many-body systems.
